# Golden interpreter checkpoint, 2026-11-08

This freezes the current universal-PyValue register interpreter as the baseline
for subsequent experiments. Golden means reproducible and correctness-qualified.
It does not imply upstream performance parity or a completed native JIT.

## Published identities

| Ref | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [`pyjit-golden-20261108-runtime`](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/tree/pyjit-golden-20261108-runtime) | Exact runtime `0765e9be47f55d97ba5d31d2ae1c02a55ea2e5ae`; origin branch `boil/pyvalue-rc-universal` |
| [`pyjit-golden-20261108`](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/tree/pyjit-golden-20261108) | The same implementation with current canonical documentation/tools under `pyjit/`, replacing the historical `boil/` documentation tree; branch `pyjit/golden-20261108` |
| `0267d428808` | Functional checkpoint used for the full suites, final timings and profiles; exact measured ELF retained locally |

Tags are immutable. The combined snapshot is for readers who need current
implementation and documentation in one checkout. Its publication checks
require all paths outside `boil/` and `pyjit/` to match the runtime commit
exactly. Publication receipts record the resolved commits and remote refs;
the canonical `weaver/python-jit` documentation branch is also pushed.

`0765e9be47f` only relocates an existing comment. The rebuilt debug `.text`
matches the measured functional checkpoint; release has four changed address
bytes pointing to equivalent `f` literals because build-identifier suffix
merging changed their locations. There is no interpreter-code change. Do not
claim identical whole ELFs or relabel old measurements as new captures.

## What is frozen

- Canonical eight-byte PyValues in interpreter homes, core containers and
  attributes; RC with cyclic collection; rebuilt bundled extensions. Direct
  value operations coexist with owning compatibility bridges where needed.
- Compiler-produced register IR with explicit slot operands and call windows,
  folded loads/stores, temporary compaction and constant homes for eligible
  loop scalars. Baseline IR is distinct from the planned optimizing SSA tier.
- Generated musttail handlers, guarded feedback/specialization, monitoring,
  frame stacking and overlapping calls, explicit ownership retirement and
  exception unwinding.
- The latest batch: typed code homes and successful-refresh cleanup
  (`0539e0c1ff9`), checked ordinary NOP continuation (`73c20472a9f`), dictionary
  first-probe identity hit (`d93b83800a5`), guarded general Python-call entry
  (`10627c339fa`), and test-interface fixes through `0267d428808`.

Read the [IR design](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/design/register-ir.md),
[interpreter design](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/design/interpreter.md),
[runtime architecture](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/design/runtime-architecture.md) and
[PyValue design](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/design/pyvalue.md). The first three include Mermaid
flow diagrams. The [historical IR reference](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/design/archive/register-ir-20261108.md)
retains earlier comparisons, proposals and decisions without presenting them
as the current specification.

## Qualification and performance

At `0267d428808`, release and debug each passed **54,394 tests, zero failures**.
Release/debug/stats check 117 modules; API lint covers 306 units with zero
failing findings. The comment-only rebuild subsequently passed the 142-test
stats smoke. Qualification covers Linux x86-64/GIL, GCC 15.2.0. The golden
documentation publication does not rerun full native suites because it changes
no implementation blobs.

The [retained report](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/bench/results/interpreter-parity-20261108.md)
is the measurement authority. JIT is explicitly disabled; compiler/build
policy is fixed. Elapsed candidate/control factors are:

| Comparison | Factor |
| --- | --- |
| Logging / upstream, two six-round campaigns | 1.387177; 1.378619 |
| 29-kernel broad screen / upstream, two rounds | 1.241158 |
| Logging / retained R5 ELF, four rounds | 0.840163 |
| 29-kernel comparison / retained R5 ELF | 0.980981 |
| Spectral / retained R5 ELF | 1.086037 |

The retained-R5 ELF comparison shares current extensions and standard library;
it is not a pristine old-source comparison. The spectral regression is accepted
for this checkpoint and must remain visible in subsequent integration screens.
Its extra counter capture shows a CPI penalty with unresolved cause. Logging's
instruction/cycle ratios against upstream are 1.434888/1.383861, suggesting
added work as the main measured distinction rather than a demonstrated cache
cause. Samples identify candidates, not additive potential savings.

All 72 stat invocations were valid; eight DWARF captures have zero lost samples.
The perf reports retain an `Invalid HEADER_EVENT_DESC` warning; stat results
are independent. Exact ELF, module, source, JIT-off and workload identities and
raw timings remain under the local evidence path in [HANDOFF](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/HANDOFF.md).
Raw build evidence is not uploaded to Git by this publication; another machine
can rebuild the source but cannot claim to possess the retained measured ELF.

## Cleanup and next work

Current navigation and design pages replace the accumulated historical boards.
The previous pages are [archived](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/archive/20261108/STATUS.md), with links
adjusted for their new locations. Sealed reviews, failed checks and measurement
records remain unchanged. Temporary instrumentation from the implementation
batch was already removed and stats rebuilt.

The [cleanup audit](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/issues/golden-20261108/cleanup-audit.md) records preserved dirty worktrees, ignored
evidence and an active build dependency. No legacy tree was established as
safe to delete. The three preexisting canonical local changes remain outside
publication. No runtime rewrite or speculative cleanup is included.

The [fresh cold review](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/issues/golden-20261108/v8-cold-review.md) assesses IR, optimization and
interpreter implementation independently. The [next plan](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/issues/golden-20261108/next-steps.md)
records its recommendations alongside accumulated evidence. Follow that plan
in separate experiments; do not move the golden tag.

# Golden runtime: independent interpreter and IR review

Reviewed 2026-11-08. Runtime tag `pyjit-golden-20261108-runtime`, commit
`0765e9be47f55d97ba5d31d2ae1c02a55ea2e5ae`. In source references below,
`R` means `/home/power/code/cpython/.worktrees/python-boil-the-ocean/build/worktrees/pyvalue-rc-universal`.
Line numbers refer to that frozen tree, not the documentation checkout's older
runtime sources. This is a source review from a V8/interpreter engineering
perspective; it claims no personal V8 employment or access to private evidence.

I read the runtime format, compiler passes, generator, calls and frame code
before reading earlier recommendation documents. I then read the new IR and
interpreter specifications and the retained performance report. There were no
runtime edits, builds, timings or new qualification runs. The applicable
[CPython AI policy](https://devguide.python.org/getting-started/ai-tools/)
was read before making recommendations. Implementation requires the project's
design and independent review process; this review approves no implementation.

## Assessment

The register interpreter is real. It directly executes explicit operands,
folds eligible local loads and stores, compacts temporaries, has typed feedback,
specialized handlers, a frame stack, and overlapping Python argument windows.
It should not be described as an upstream stack interpreter with different
names. Nor is it an optimizing SSA IR: joins use canonical stack-position
homes, windows constrain allocation, and source observation constrains motion.
`R/Include/internal/pycore_regcfg.h:14` documents those choices precisely.

The architecture has sound ownership discipline but makes physical execution
carry several logical contracts: instruction boundaries, source events,
ownership retirement, and reconstruction of a stack model for debugger jumps.
That coupling leaves meaningful work even after a handler dispatch disappears.
The highest-value next work is to separate those contracts enough to eliminate
unneeded execution, while keeping their proofs explicit. Another broad call
transaction rewrite or a new word encoding is not yet justified.

Python requires observable locals, correct exception attribution, reentrant
finalizers, monitoring and generator behavior. It does **not** require every
source boundary to occupy an executable word, every child argument to own an
independent count, or every consumed home to be cleared immediately when no
observer can read it. Those are current implementation choices. Replacing any
one requires replacing its consumers' assumptions, not declaring it redundant.

The measurement evidence is consistent with this diagnosis but does not prove
an attribution. Logging retires 1.4349 times upstream's instructions and uses
1.3839 times its cycles per unchanged workload loop. The latest batch reduced
entered handlers from 161 to 151 while retaining 20 frames; ten NOP words remain
and nine result POPs remain. Samples locate work in overlap preparation,
cleanup, calls, returns and lookups; their self shares cannot be added as a
removable-time budget. These are existing results from the
[checkpoint report](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/bench/results/interpreter-parity-20261108.md), not
measurements made for this review. The accepted spectral regression remains a
required screening workload.

## What the V8 and LuaJIT comparisons actually support

Pinned V8 reference: tag **13.0.245**, commit
`4be854bd71ea878a25b236a27afcecffa2e29360`. This deliberately uses a fixed source
revision, not an assertion about today's V8. Ignition's register optimizer
tracks equivalence and materialization and flushes live register state; its
baseline bytecodes are not the optimizing compiler's phi graph.
See [register optimizer, especially Flush](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/4be854bd71ea878a25b236a27afcecffa2e29360/src/interpreter/bytecode-register-optimizer.cc#L322)
and the separate [bytecode graph builder's loop phis](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/4be854bd71ea878a25b236a27afcecffa2e29360/src/compiler/bytecode-graph-builder.cc#L788).
This supports keeping a cheap executable baseline and a separate optimizing
representation; it does not support importing global SSA passes into dispatch.

V8 records source positions in a side table, but its bytecode writer still
limits elision when source information conflicts and invalidates elision state
at exception-region boundaries. Metadata therefore helps; it does not erase
the semantic problem. See [source position emission and bounded elision](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/4be854bd71ea878a25b236a27afcecffa2e29360/src/interpreter/bytecode-array-writer.cc#L167).

Ignition has general register-list calls and small known-arity call handlers;
both use call machinery and collect feedback. That supports specializing
frequent call shapes, not a claim that JavaScript calls have no checks or
frame work. See [JSCall and JSCallN](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/4be854bd71ea878a25b236a27afcecffa2e29360/src/interpreter/interpreter-generator.cc#L1310).

Pinned LuaJIT reference: v2.1 commit
`c5a2fa4df71eb5ee9c71bc7b32bb5630d18568d7`. Its trace snapshots map changed slots
and carry restoration distinctions; those maps belong to trace recovery, not
to a general license to leave arbitrary interpreter homes stale. See
[snapshot_slots](https://github.com/LuaJIT/LuaJIT/blob/c5a2fa4df71eb5ee9c71bc7b32bb5630d18568d7/src/lj_snap.c#L56).
Neither comparison transfers tracing-GC root rules or delayed collection to
Python's reference-count and finalizer semantics.

## Ranked recommendations

Ranking weighs concrete covered work, implementation cost, semantic risk and
how cheaply an experiment can reject the idea. It is not a speedup forecast.
The entries are distinct alternatives; several may ultimately share metadata.

### 1. Finish dead call-result lowering across the return boundary

**Implemented:** `IR_NO_DST`, call discard flags and return-side discard are
already present. **Missing:** the compiler retains a final `POP_TOP` when it
alone preserves the call's line after control returns. The reason is explicit
in `R/Python/regcfg_passes.c:620–655`: tracing can start inside the callee, so
the next word must still expose the caller's call line. This is an observation
constraint, not a use of the returned value by Python code.

**Change:** represent the post-call observation/retirement point separately
enough to let the returning path deliver directly to a discard recipient.
Preserve the ordering of line callbacks and result destruction. Do not simply
delete POP or close the result early. The recipient slot is on the **caller**:
`R/Python/bytecodes.c:5549` and
`R/Include/internal/pycore_interpframe.h:169`.
The existing Python return holds its result in a C owner, restores the caller
as current, retires the child, and only then publishes or discards that result
(`R/Python/generated_ir_cases.c.h:16015–16060`). Child-cleanup finalizers run
before the destination changes; the new lowering must preserve this ordering.

**Covered work:** nine retained result POP handler entries in the measured
logging loop, plus eligible other callers. The result's required release
remains. No numeric elapsed saving is established. **Cost/risk:** medium;
debugger activation and finalizer order dominate the proof.

**Smallest experiment:** lower one eligible call/POP form with an explicit
post-return boundary description. First compare instruction/event sequences
and owner retirements, then inspect generated code and per-workload handler
counts. Reject if maintaining the boundary merely recreates equivalent work.
**Gate:** tracing activated inside the callee; line/opcode monitoring toggled
there; callbacks that mutate locals or raise; a returned last-reference object
whose finalizer inspects the caller; discard to native and Python callees;
exceptions and frame escape. Broader performance screening follows only after
these semantics agree.

### 2. Make logical source boundaries independent of executable NOP words

**Implemented:** the boolean-false specialization can execute one ordinary
live NOP inline. It still tests that word and publishes its PC:
`R/Python/ceval_macros.h:741–760`,
`R/Python/bytecodes.c:3488,3533`, and the checked generator rule at
`R/Tools/cases_generator/ir_generator.py:3669`. Wrapped targets, lltrace and
free-threaded execution decline that shortcut. Calling this “NOP removal” is
inaccurate. **Missing:** a logical-boundary map independent of execution words.

**Change:** keep a logical position/event identity and map it to a resume
position and required state. A boundary may be on an edge, including a taken
edge, rather than on the following instruction. Multiple boundaries at one
physical PC need ordering; a source line number alone cannot represent them.
The ordinary path should not decode a NOP just to discover an empty action.
Instrumentation can use mapped boundary handlers or another reviewed slow
path, without requiring a dormant executable word at every boundary.

This cannot be accomplished by editing the line table alone. Today:

- `R/Include/internal/pycore_ir.h:65` makes lasti, line and exception offsets
  word indices; jump encoding and assembler relaxation use that coordinate.
- `R/Python/instrumentation.c:58–135` patches handler words and indexes
  monitoring data by word, including destinations and relaxed jumps.
- `R/Objects/frameobject.c:1648` reconstructs stack kinds from executed IR
  formats for `f_lineno`; folded inputs and elided NULLs already need special
  reconstruction rules.
- `R/Python/regcfg_passes.c:70,169,534,1195` preserves line and stack-shape
  boundaries during several different transformations.

**Covered work:** residual NOP word checks/PC writes, remaining ordinary NOP
dispatch elsewhere, and constraints that retain otherwise removable code.
The ten logging NOPs already avoid their own dispatch; do not claim ten more
dispatches can be saved there. **Cost/risk:** large for a general solution,
medium for a bounded first boundary kind; debugger jumps and dynamic monitoring
are the main risks.

**Smallest experiment:** create a compile-time census of NOP reasons and their
incoming edges, then prototype only the existing boolean continuation using
an edge boundary record. Compare physical word count and generated hot-path
instructions. **Gate:** exact event order, lasti/traceback attribution, exception
range endpoints, forward/backward/taken/fallthrough edges, tracing enabled
during a callee or callback, f_lineno legal/illegal jumps, generators and
monitoring changes while suspended. Preserve a single selected representation
if adopted; a temporary experiment is not a permanent dual architecture.

### 3. Encode frequent operand ownership modes once, instead of rediscovering them in each handler

**Implemented:** local-versus-temporary class is fixed by field index; the
compiler knows it. **Missing:** many generated handlers still test that class
at runtime through `IR_IS_LOCAL`, `IR_CONSUME_INPUT`, `IR_STORE_DST` and related
macros (`R/Python/ceval_macros.h:498–641`). This is distinct from borrowing
arguments across calls: even under today's owning-home policy, the same
instruction's operand mode does not vary between executions.

**Change:** assess a small number of generated handler variants for the most
frequent input/destination modes. Select them after slot allocation, and make
their deopt/instrumentation mappings explicit. Avoid the Cartesian product of
all types, modes and families. A side-table load or branch can cost as much as
the current comparison; packing new bits is not automatically better.

**Covered work:** repeated slot-class comparisons, conditional consumption,
and local/temp output paths in admitted handlers. Dynamic value-tag tests that
remain semantically necessary are outside this saving. **Cost/risk:** medium;
handler text growth and mapping mistakes are the principal costs.

**Smallest experiment:** census operand modes for one hot scalar reader,
generate only its dominant mode, and inspect compiled instructions/text size
before timing. **Gate:** local/temporary aliasing, deopt before consumption,
instrumented twins, finalizer mutation of folded destinations, error cleanup,
and canonical result publication. Require a broad screen including spectral;
fewer branches with larger text is not necessarily a win.

### 4. Minimize frame entry and retirement on the actual exact and general routes

**Implemented:** exact positional calls already bypass the transaction helper:
`R/Python/generated_ir_cases.c.h:7186` executes `CALL_PY_EXACT_ARGS` with its own
guards and `_PyFrame_PushOverlapping`. The guarded general path is separate at
`R/Python/ceval.c:3376`; its overlap preparation is at `3055`. Initialization
still performs the general frame-header protocol
(`R/Include/internal/pycore_interpframe.h:282`), and ordinary cleanup is already
locals-only (`R/Python/frame.c:185`). **Missing:** an attributable hot entry/
retirement cost model and a proof of which remaining header/guard work can
be moved to code preparation or observation slow paths.

**Change:** evaluate a validated call-entry descriptor containing immutable
code-layout facts, and a minimal synchronous entry/return sequence using it.
Keep dynamic function/provider/recursion/stack guards. Consider lazy derivation
of observer-only header data only after a consumer census proves it safe.
Do not remove code ownership merely because the function also owns its current
code: `__code__` can change while an older activation is running.

**Covered work:** recurring header setup, code/layout reloads and retirement,
on whichever route compiled-code inspection actually identifies. This does
not save binder copies in logging: the retained diagnostics found none.
General-path post-kwargs revalidation is necessary after an allocation that
can run Python, not redundant by inspection. GCC may already combine repeated
loads in exact-call source; source duplication is not machine-code evidence.
**Cost/risk:** medium to large; frame introspection and entry failures are hard.

A bounded read-only inspection of the retained spectral candidate ELF
(`spectral-perf-identities/candidate-python`, GNU build ID
`d70c9143464a2fb1efeb488c5609c502cc4e5caf`) confirms this is worth inspecting:
`objdump -d --disassemble=_TAIL_CALL_CALL_PY_EXACT_ARGS` shows a 48-byte C stack
allocation and several stack stores/reloads in its entry sequence. This does
not prove that any particular spill is avoidable or explain spectral's loss.
It supports an emitted-code experiment, not source-only claims about the
tail-call convention. Keep GCC fixed; compare hot/cold factoring and live
state across the existing calling convention before proposing another backend.

**Smallest experiment:** use the retained exact/general route counts and
disassembly to count stores, loads and owner operations separately for each
entry/return shape. Prototype a descriptor for one no-default exact shape
only if it removes demonstrated work. **Gate:** mutated `__code__`, defaults
and vectorcall; PEP 523; recursion/stack exhaustion; frame exposure and GC
during preparation; exceptions before commit; generator-owned callers;
monitoring activated during preparation. An exact-entry improvement must be
measured on the inner exact route, not credited from the P3 general route.

### 5. Test borrowed synchronous child arguments as an independent ownership design

**Implemented:** argument-window overlap transfers owners into child homes;
it already avoids an argument-array copy. Strong local loads used as call
arguments can still create counts, and the child retires its owning locals.
See `R/Include/internal/pycore_interpframe.h:526` and
`R/Python/bytecodes.c:4318`. **Missing:** mortal borrowed frame homes, anchor
identity, overwrite/escape promotion, GC edge accounting and consumer support.

**Change:** assess a representation where an eligible child argument names an
explicit surviving owner. Preserve canonical heap PyValues; borrowing is a
frame ownership property, not an alternate heap value format. Universal
eight-byte values do not themselves require a fresh child count.

**Covered work:** only mortal argument increment/decrement pairs that this
proof admits. Inline/immortal arguments, already transferred temporary owners,
and required result/kwargs destruction provide no corresponding saving.
Logging's 90 increments/100 decrements per loop are an aggregate, not the
borrowable-argument budget. **Cost/risk:** large; a hidden owner dependency can
break GC subtraction, cycles, frame escape and native transfer.

**Smallest experiment:** count argument provenance and surviving owner identity
on exact and general routes without changing ownership. Derive a ledger of
candidate removable pairs. If small, stop; if substantial, build one explicit
anchor/promotion design. **Gate:** deleting/rebinding the parent local;
callee argument overwrite; recursion; frame escape; generators; native calls
that steal ownership; callback mutation; GC cycles and incoming-edge counting;
ordinary guard decline and error paths. No fallback may observe an unanchored
borrow or consume it as an owner. This is worth investigating but is not the
only credible next direction.

### 6. Extend generated contracts into checked guard, heap-effect and phase facts

**Implemented:** metadata derives reads/writes, callback/raise/poll effects,
borrowable inputs and a narrow first-output publication phase. Shape checks
for the new bool, dict and guarded call paths are deliberately strict
(`R/Tools/cases_generator/ir_generator.py:3669–3801,4304–4770`).
**Missing:** general heap read/write domains, guard-established facts and
multi-output/error phase contracts; `R/Include/internal/pycore_ir.h:254`
explicitly says so. Copy propagation consequently respects a family's union
of possible Python callbacks (`R/Python/regcfg_passes.c:155–306`).

**Change:** add semantic declarations only for optimizations that need them:
guard before effects; possible callback/heap write; output ownership and
publication; decline preserves inputs; error cleanup. Derive consumer tables
from those declarations. Retain conservative default effects for unknown
helpers. Strict token-shape validation is a useful safety mechanism today;
relaxing it without a replacement proof would be a regression.

**Covered work:** duplicated synchronization/publication and overly broad
barriers in certified paths, plus safer reuse by future optimizing frontends.
A generic IR op cannot assume its warmed specialization will always run;
moving a local read across it needs a guard and correct fallback state.
**Cost/risk:** medium to large; false purity is a correctness bug.

**Smallest experiment:** describe one existing two-output method reader and
its success/decline/error states, then show one redundant operation the
generated contract can remove. **Gate:** negative generator tests for missing
effects and invalid phase promises; callbacks between outputs; destination
aliasing; receiver/displaced-owner finalizers; guard failures after an effect;
monitoring and exceptions. Do not turn a single success-path result fact into
a GC root or whole-handler purity claim.

### 7. Replace the universal NULL-home invariant only with an ownership/validity map

**Implemented:** consumption clears temporary cells and outputs publish valid
homes; overlap initialization already skips the known-NULL shared tail.
**Missing:** persistent validity/occupied-owner state independent of physical
bits. GC scans every physical slot (`R/Python/gc.c:483`); frame copying moves
every slot (`R/Include/internal/pycore_interpframe.h:224`); exception cleanup
releases temporaries in reverse slot order (`:198`). Compaction's future-read
liveness is not sufficient for any of those consumers.

**Change:** first try bounded coalescing of clear-and-overwrite within a proven
non-reentrant sequence. If that cannot cover enough work, assess an explicit
map that distinguishes valid slots, owned references and future reads at each
observation/cleanup point. Preserve release ordering and account for C-owned
values. Never expose stale bits as another owning edge or drop a no-future-read
owner that still requires retirement.

**Covered work:** selected NULL writes, initialization and scans; ordinary
normal cleanup already avoids scanning transfer temporaries. Logging's zero
constant homes mean constant-home initialization cannot explain its gap.
**Cost/risk:** small for a verified local pair, very large for general maps.

**Smallest experiment:** count adjacent consume-clear/overwrite pairs with no
callback, allocation, release, poll or observer between them; prototype one
coalesced form while keeping valid homes at all exits. **Gate:** allocating
and last-reference release paths, unwinding, GC, frame copy/escape, infinite
loops with owners lacking future reads, generators, monitoring and lltrace.
General maps require a complete consumer census before changing initialization.

### 8. Use polymorphic feedback to improve execution only where alternating sites justify it

**Implemented:** feedback records up to four observations, then MEGA; it also
helps select a non-shape attribute fallback. **Missing:** a general bounded
polymorphic execution chain; ordinary handlers still execute the selected
current specialization. See `R/Include/internal/pycore_feedback.h:49–58`,
`R/Python/specialize.c:354–559,876`. Recording a POLY state is not itself a
polymorphic inline cache.

**Change:** experiment with a two-entry guarded execution path for one family
where repeated deopts and respecializations are demonstrated. Keep raw cached
pointers borrowed and guarded by the owning type/version protocol; do not
equate a recorded type version with a proven guard.

**Covered work:** repeated guard misses and specialization churn in admitted
alternating sites. There is no evidence this helps the warmed monomorphic
logging target. **Cost/risk:** medium; larger handlers and stale-cache safety.

**Smallest experiment:** a two-shape attribute workload plus a real broader
workload with recorded misses; compare misses, retired instructions and text
growth with the monomorphic policy. **Gate:** descriptor precedence, deletion,
type/version invalidation, class mutation, callbacks, MEGA transition and
instrumentation. Branch-history writes are a separate policy: the runtime
currently records them under specialization, even with the JIT disabled
(`R/Python/ceval_macros.h:366`). Any sampling change must identify its consumers
and freshness contract; removing history because the JIT is off is not this
PIC experiment.

### 9. Keep optimizing SSA and backend work separate, but share semantic lowering and recovery contracts

**Implemented:** executable register IR plus generated C/musttail dispatch.
**Missing:** native method/trace SSA execution, hardware allocation, OSR and
general recovery. The current [JIT design](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/design/jit-e2e-system.md)
explicitly labels its Action/recovery interface as unimplemented. The presence
of a native publication/unwind utility does not establish a working optimizing
tier.

**Change:** use one semantic lowering contract for methods and traces, with
explicit effects and reconstructible state, while keeping baseline words cheap.
Start recovery with a bounded before-effect exit; then add after-effect/error
states without replaying callbacks or releases. Do not make the baseline word
format carry every future SSA fact, or treat opcode-to-uop expansion as a
complete frontend. Backend register allocation is distinct from frame-slot
compaction.

**Covered work:** future repeated guards, boxed/general operations, frame
traffic and loops that a native optimizer can eliminate. It saves **nothing**
in the current JIT-disabled measurements. **Cost/risk:** very large; recovery
and owner lifetime, not merely instruction selection, are the admission cost.

**Smallest experiment:** lower one pure arithmetic/control region to the
shared typed graph, force a before-effect exit at every guard, and compare the
reconstructed interpreter state and owners. **Gate:** exact fault/resume PC,
inline-frame and locals reconstruction, ownership and GC accounting, exception
state, tooling/unwind metadata, and no repeated effects. Later call/return and
trace side exits extend this gate; they cannot inherit it by assertion.

## Current specification review

The new short specifications are substantially more useful than a dated
multi-thousand-line design ledger. The following findings were made against
their drafts, using the frozen source. **All nine are resolved** in the current
`pyjit/design/register-ir.md` and `interpreter.md`, re-read after the final
return-order correction at 23:24 UTC. These are documentation findings, not
runtime bugs:

1. **Dispatch:** the interpreter draft describes a selected computed-goto or
   tail-call configuration. Frozen `R/Python/ceval_macros.h:44,108–115` has
   function-per-handler musttail dispatch. Describe that one backend.
2. **Return destination:** the return recipient's `return_slot` is on the
   caller, not the dying child. See `R/Python/bytecodes.c:5549` and
   `R/Include/internal/pycore_interpframe.h:169`.
3. **Constants:** hidden homes cover eligible inline scalar constants used by
   borrowable loop readers, not every constant. Constants outside loops and
   window inputs keep their loads (`R/Python/regcfg_passes.c:794`). Hidden
   constants sit between cells and free variables, not after all freevars.
4. **Producer ordering:** the optimized flowgraph already removes pseudo-ops
   and normalizes jumps before register conversion (`R/Python/regcfg.c:6`).
5. **Coordinates:** include fused compare/contains/is branches' signed D
   relative encoding as well as FOR_ITER/SEND. CD's numeric value is
   `C | (D << 12)`; the draft's “C:D” wording can suggest the opposite order.
6. **Sharing:** clarify that the executing copy is per code object, shared by
   frames and also threads in the free-threaded build; “private” means separate
   from immutable words. Free-threaded specialization is disabled
   (`R/Include/internal/pycore_ir.h:328`, `R/Python/ir.c:452`).
7. **Narrow continuation:** say the NOP shortcut is in the checked
   `POP_JUMP_IF_FALSE_BOOL` continuation. It is not a general scan of every
   dispatch target, as a broad flowchart arrow could imply.
8. **Calls:** distinguish exact direct entry from general guarded overlap and
   consuming fallback. The exact path does not first execute the general
   resource-preparation transaction. Preserve the as-built route distinction.
9. **Return order:** hold the owned result in C while making the caller current
   and retiring the child, then publish/discard to the recipient. The initial
   prose and diagram reversed retirement and publication. Cleanup can run
   Python, so this distinction changes what a finalizer observes. See
   `R/Python/generated_ir_cases.c.h:16015–16060` and
   `R/Python/ceval_macros.h:763`.

The coordinator applied the corrections while preparing the documents. The
register-IR diagram still uses “private executing copy” as shorthand, but its
execution-copy section now explicitly defines per-code sharing, so the
ownership meaning is clear.

The final return prose and call diagram now explicitly hold the owned result
across child cleanup and publish/discard afterward. I also read the
[coordinator's next plan](https://github.com/rjpower/cpython/blob/pyjit-golden-20261108/pyjit/issues/golden-20261108/next-steps.md): its nine dispositions accurately
reflect this review, keep borrowing independent, preserve the two separate
call routes, and add child-cleanup finalizer ordering to the acceptance gate.
There are no remaining source-accuracy blockers in those pages from this
bounded review. The coordinator owns rendered-diagram inspection and final
publication; this review checked their text and control-flow meaning.

Review verification was source/retained-artifact inspection and whitespace
checks. Runtime HEAD and its clean working-tree status were checked again;
no runtime file was changed. The proposed semantic gates above are future
admission requirements, not tests executed by this review.

## Suggested next packet

Start with the first three entries as separate designs: return/discard
boundaries, logical source anchors, and one measured operand-mode variant.
In parallel with design work, derive the exact/general call cost ledger and
the borrowable-argument ledger from existing evidence or bounded diagnostics.
Choose implementation only after each experiment's removable-work budget and
semantic proof are concrete. This preserves borrowing as a serious option
without allowing a previously selected plan to decide the review's conclusion.

Do not bundle a new word format, global root maps, borrowed homes and JIT
recovery into one interpreter optimization. Their proofs overlap, but their
costs and failure modes need separate decisions. Keep the frozen baseline,
unchanged logging workload and broad spectral screen for subsequent comparisons.

> Canonical source: `pyjit/issues/interpreter-parity-20261108/alternatives-review.md`. Proposals require coordinator selection and independent review; runtime remains qualified R5. The fresh pinned logging baseline is 1.657289x upstream. Supporting relative links refer to the canonical checkout.

# Architectural alternatives before selecting the next batch

2026-11-08. Independent second pass over runtime `0953757f4e7`, canonical
contracts, the eight V8 recommendations and the coordinator's warmed logging
capture. Source review only: no builds, tests, native workloads, counters or
benchmarks. The user requested this comparison before implementation priority
is selected. Earlier source approval of the small refresh/code-home changes
does not select them, or the specialized call route, as the next architecture.

## Decision to make

The retained target factor is 1.743034, so matching that upstream measurement
would require about 42.6% less candidate elapsed time. Two tiny cleanups and a
future-JIT boundary do not explain how to close that gap. Neither samples nor
source establish a savings budget for any mechanism below. Even a correct
implementation that removes visible checks can be immaterial.

Compare six mechanisms on the same target and call/non-call controls. This is
a choice among changes to the interpreter's work, generated C, compiler and
instruction interface; it is not a choice between universal values and a
return to boxed heap fields. GCC stays fixed, JIT stays off, and reference
counting, observer behavior and canonical owning homes remain requirements.

The warmed capture supplies unusually useful discrimination. Its 67-word
outer body has ten method loads, ten `CALL_PY_GENERAL` sites, ten argument
`LOAD_FAST_BORROW` sites in the repeated body, and ten result `POP_TOP`s.
The 18-word `Logger.debug` body has a method load and `CALL_PY_EXACT_ARGS` on
the silent route. `isEnabledFor`'s first nine words contain two shape reads,
boolean branching, cached dict subscription and returns; most of its 72 words
belong to other paths. Static counts for the whole function must not be used
as dynamic hot-path denominators. Route outcomes, escape counts and native
instructions still need separate diagnostic evidence.

| Mechanism | Logging coverage hypothesis | Broader coverage | First discrimination | Migration risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. Fact-carrying call entry and shared preparation | High at outer calls; does not remove inner exact entry cost | Defaulted/variadic Python calls, both bound and unbound after separate proofs | Reconcile route counts and pre/post-escape checks | Medium |
| B. Phase-aware state publication and leaf paths | High across method/shape loads, cache read, return and call continuation | Attribute/item/arithmetic-heavy code | Count actual publications, refreshes and escapes on the hot prefix | Medium; high if line boundaries are fused |
| C. Ownership-aware equivalence and window construction | Directly targets repeated argument snapshot/window words | Call construction, expressions, unpack/build windows | Explain every surviving transfer in warmed IR | Medium to high |
| D. Operand-class specialization or layout revision | Potentially broad across short handlers; existing window operands are already temporaries | Nearly all register operations | Count surviving class branches in release GCC | Medium for handler forms; high for encoding |
| E. Dispatch interface, fusion and word density | Broad across all hot words, including ten caller POPs | Dispatch-heavy loops and large instruction streams | Normalize state spills and dispatches; distinguish cache pressure from instruction work | Medium for one fusion; high for interface/format |
| F. Frame entry/retirement and constant-home policy | Both Python frames per disabled logging call | All short Python calls and generators | Count actual initialization/clear/constant work by call shape | Medium for one typed field; high for validity-map changes |

These are coverage rankings, not expected-speedup rankings. A, B and F all
touch the same calls and their savings cannot be added as independent shares.
C and E can remove the same dispatch. D can change register pressure and
erase gains elsewhere. Native recovery remains deferred under recommendation
8 because it cannot contribute to a JIT-off result.

## A. Preserve facts through a shared call preparation/commit

Recommendations 1 and part of 4. Source:
`generated_ir_cases.c.h:CALL_PY_GENERAL`,
`specialize.c:specialize_py_call`, `funcobject.c:PyFunction_SetVectorcall`, and
`ceval.c:call_transaction_invoke/call_transaction_overlap_python`.

Competing designs are (1) carry only the already established method-prepared
fact through the existing scalar call interface; (2) add an explicit private
guarded Python entry sharing the preparation/commit implementation with the
generic entry; (3) replace generic preparation with a wider persistent call
plan. The third has greater state and invalidation cost and is unsupported
until the first two identify a material limit. A new general call ABI or
opcode-name table is unnecessary.

Under the held GIL, successful type/version/PEP guards imply standard Python
entry before an escape; the public vectorcall setter clears the cached
version. Provider rediscovery before that escape is optional. After kwargs
allocation, callable/code/provider/hook/executable/capacity/defaults/self
mapping must be revalidated. Fresh kwargs, defaults ownership, recursion,
monitoring and clearable child publication remain real work. The nonallocating
shortcut does not cover `Logger.debug` and the warmed inner call is already
exact, so it is a poor leading logging hypothesis without new route evidence.

Smallest experiment: first count mutually exclusive entry/outcome shapes and
the allocations/refreshes within accepted overlap calls. Inspect GCC for the
specific pre-escape duplication that a private entry would remove. Then
compare one private entry with the smaller prepared-bit variant, keeping
the same shared commit. Test the generated fallback label separately: it must
retain generic entry whenever guards did not complete. Bound-method retirement,
monitoring and free-threaded paths cannot inherit the unbound proof.

Reject as the next major mechanism if the targeted route is uncommon, GCC
already eliminates the duplication, the entry merely moves spills, or the
post-allocation/entry work dominates and the target/control screen shows no
repeatable benefit. Correctness failure on mutation, setter, allocation,
monitoring or fallback rejects the implementation regardless of speed.

## B. Publish state at actual escape phases; make proven leaf paths small

Recommendations 3–4, with a larger scope than one duplicate refresh. Source:
`ir_generator.py:prepare_call/call_reload/reader_reload/IRStack.store`,
`ceval.c:value_operation_refresh`,
`bytecodes.c:LOAD_ATTR_SHAPE/LOAD_ATTR_METHOD_WITH_VALUES`, and the existing
first-output publication contract.

Competing designs are (1) remove individual duplicate stores/checks; (2) have
the shared generator carry checked phase facts such as PC already published,
result canonical in a temporary, and no escape since decoding; (3) generate
paired leaf/escaping continuations for selected handlers. A transitive leaf
proof must include releases and local displacement: a dictionary read or
attribute result may be simple while retiring its receiver can run Python.
Do not replace one conservative whole-handler flag with scattered optimistic
annotations. Use the generated contract and invalidate phase facts at escapes.

The logging hot prefix makes this a real competitor to call entry. It has
method lookup, shape-home results and a warmed dictionary read on every silent
path, including the inner exact-call route that A does not simplify. A result
that is inline or immortal may avoid a release callback, but that is a value
fact to check or prove, not a property of all attribute lookups. Observable
local publication and post-callback refresh remain required. Generic scalar
canonicalization at known-code entry is a narrow instance, not the whole idea.

Smallest experiment: map one actual shape-read → cache-subscription → return
prefix into phases. Count published PC/home stores, actual escaping calls,
receiver/displaced-owner releases and refreshes separately. Inspect GCC to
see which state reloads survive. Propose a single generator rule that removes
only unchanged state traffic, with explicit invalidation and generic fallback.
Compare it with the smallest local C simplification on the same prefix.

Reject if all apparent redundancy follows genuine escapes, if the leaf guard
cost exceeds saved traffic, or if the generated rule needs per-handler hidden
exceptions. Callback mutation, exception ownership, tracing and folded-local
destinations are decisive tests. A tiny isolated cleanup may still be useful,
but cannot serve as evidence for broad phase-contract benefit.

## C. Change compiler equivalence/window construction rather than call entry

Recommendations 5 and part of 6. Source:
`regcfg_passes.c:_PyRegPass_CopyProp`, `regcfg.c:compact_op` and the window
verifier. The compiler already folds borrowable single-reader local loads,
kills pending loads across possible Python execution/local writes, and tracks
occupancy until consumption rather than future-read liveness alone.

Competing designs are (1) improve equivalence inside the current same-line,
nonescaping regions; (2) choose destination windows earlier so producers write
directly into their final owning argument homes; (3) allow calls to gather
arguments from independent registers or locals. The third removes contiguity
as an encoding constraint but loses simple zero-copy child overlap and must
make evaluated owning snapshots before any fallible/reentrant step. A gather
list is not automatically cheaper than today's argument window.

The target retains one message-local-to-window word per outer call. It may be
the necessary snapshot under the current instruction interface, not allocator
waste. The method loader already writes callable/self into the window. There
is no broad copy chain in the warmed nine-word `isEnabledFor` hot prefix; its
many COPY/SWAP words are mostly elsewhere. That weakens a compiler-only route
to parity here while leaving broader call-expression coverage plausible.

Smallest experiment: annotate every surviving load/move as evaluation snapshot,
contiguity, line/observer barrier, retirement-order preservation or avoidable
pass limitation. Identify a producer that could target its final window home
without changing release time, then compare emitted words and GCC. If the
only candidate is the message snapshot, first compare the cost of its current
word with a call form that duplicates that local into the same owner slot
inside the call; this saves a dispatch, not the necessary owner acquisition.

Reject if no avoidable transfers remain on the actual hot path, or if gather/
coalescing adds more ownership work or loses overlap. Frame-local mutation,
argument evaluation order, exception unwind and dead-but-owned temporaries
must remain correct. Last future read never licenses early local destruction.

## D. Encode or specialize operand class

Recommendation 6. Source: `pycore_ir.h`'s full 64-bit budget and
`ceval_macros.h:IR_IS_LOCAL/IR_CONSUME_INPUT/IR_STORE_DST`.

Competing designs are (1) retain words and let generated handlers specialize
the relevant source/destination classes; (2) encode class bits by trading
handler or operand range; (3) use feedback/side metadata to avoid that trade.
The first spends code/handler footprint and specialization complexity; the
second changes assembler, decoder, limits, instrumentation and readers; the
third adds a load and may cost more than the comparison it removes.

Slot class and value ownership tag are different. Class specialization can
remove a branch or address/header load; it cannot remove a mortal count,
canonicalization, local-retirement callback or evaluated call snapshot.
Window temporaries already give stronger class knowledge than arbitrary
register operands, so calls may be a weak direct beneficiary. Short shape,
dict and arithmetic handlers offer wider coverage.

Smallest experiment: choose the most frequent hot handler with a real
remaining local/temporary test in GCC, enumerate its observed class combinations,
and compare a generated fixed-class variant before revising any word bits.
Measure instruction reduction against code footprint and spills. Only a
material result justifies a range/large-function and instrumented-handler
migration proposal.

Reject if tests already fold away, class variants proliferate, new branches/
metadata loads replace the same work, or footprint/control regressions exceed
the target gain. A handler-interface improvement can be kept without implying
that the whole IR format must change.

## E. Reduce dispatch/state-interface cost and assess density separately

Recommendation 7 and the phase contract in 4. Source:
`ceval_macros.h:TAIL_CALL_PARAMS`, `ir_generator.py:call_completion`, and
`regcfg_passes.c:discard_region`.

Competing designs are (1) preserve fixed words and reduce C helper boundaries/
state pressure; (2) fuse common semantic sequences with explicit observation
boundaries; (3) change the dispatch interface or use compact/scaled words.
The current GCC convention passes five state arguments but does not assign
them permanent hardware registers. More inlining can remove an ABI transition
while increasing code size and register pressure. Compact words can reduce
instruction-stream footprint while adding decoding and complicating rewriting;
the small hot logging bodies do not by themselves demonstrate a density limit.

A concrete missed target coverage is important: all ten outer call results
still have `POP_TOP`. Discard support exists, but `discard_region` deliberately
keeps the POP when it ends the call's line. If tracing starts inside the
callee, the first caller line event must still identify that call line. Blind
POP removal is wrong. An observer-aware call-return continuation or fused
call/discard form could represent this boundary explicitly and remove normal
dispatch/result traffic while retaining activation and exceptional behavior.
This is materially broader than the prepared-bit call change, and riskier.

Smallest experiment: count hot dispatches, spills/reloads at call/return and
the actual cost of the retained POP continuation. Write an explicit two-PC/
line-boundary recipe for one call-discard pair, including tracing enabled
inside the callee, before proposing a fused handler. Compare that against
reducing one helper boundary without changing instruction/observer semantics.
Use instruction/cache evidence to decide whether density deserves a separate
experiment; do not infer it from byte width alone.

Reject fusion if it merely hides a second dispatch or needs special logging
knowledge, or if observer activation cannot recover exactly the retained
boundary. Reject a dispatch/interface rewrite if spills move elsewhere or
fixed-GCC controls regress. Density is rejected as the near-term explanation
if the hot stream fits and measured front-end evidence shows no material
pressure; noisy cache counters alone do not establish it.

## F. Revisit frame work through validity and retirement contracts

Recommendation 2, the frame-entry comparison and part of 4. Source:
`pycore_interpframe.h:_PyFrame_Initialize/_PyFrame_PushOverlapping`,
`frame.c:_PyFrame_ClearExceptCode`, and `bytecodes.c:_RETURN_VALUE`.

Competing designs are (1) keep canonical frame homes and specialize typed
fields/known-valid ranges; (2) change constant access/placement to reduce
per-entry hidden-home filling; (3) introduce initialized/owned range metadata
so entry, exposure, GC and unwind need not treat every physical slot as valid.
The third is a genuine architectural migration and cannot be approximated by
using future-read liveness. Locals, GC, frame copying and exception consumers
would all need one coherent validity contract before initialization is skipped.

The current frame stack, argument overlap, known-NULL reuse and locals-only
normal thread cleanup already exist. There is no second full-slot scan to
remove on ordinary return. Frame headers, code/function owners, live argument
owners, fresh kwargs lifetime, constants and observable local destruction
remain work. A typed code constructor removes impossible scalar checks, not
the executable owner. Changing constant placement trades entry stores for
loads/dispatch forms and must include mortal `code.replace` constants.

The constant-placement alternatives deserve their own comparison. Today a
hoisted `CO_FAST_CONST` occupies a hidden frame-local home, filled at entry
and visited by normal local clearing. An alternative can read the existing
code-owned canonical `co_consts` pool directly, with a constant operand class
or a generated handler form; another can retain frame homes but initialize a
proved constant range only at its first required phase. The former trades
per-frame fill/clear and footprint for constant-base decoding/loads, additional
operand forms and borrow-proof obligations. It need not add a competing value
representation or a second constant pool. The latter adds validity state and
observer/exception complexity and may merely move the same stores.

Code ownership is separable from constant placement. A frame's executable
owner can keep its code and `co_consts` alive while a constant operand is
borrowed; the ordinary consumer must still duplicate a mortal value whenever
it needs a new owner. `code.replace` creates another code object and can install
mortal or mutable constant objects. Preserve the active frame's original
code/pool, finalization order, cyclic traversal and hidden-versus-exposed locals
rules. Do not assume constants are immortal, or use an unowned pointer from a
replaceable function code field. A proposal must audit every consumer that
currently treats hidden constant slots as ordinary initialized homes.

Coverage is currently unresolved, and source narrows it sharply. The compiler
`regcfg_passes.c:_PyRegPass_ConstSlots` nominates loads only in backward-jump
loop blocks and returns without hoisting when there are none. Neither warmed
logging callee has a backward jump. The JSON records source `nlocals` values
4 and 3, but omits `co_nlocalsplus`, total slots and `co_nconstslots`; it does
not establish any per-call hidden-constant cost here. Obtain all four counts,
the actual constant-slot table and known-NULL overlap prefix before claiming
that cold regions enlarge entry work. A zero constant-slot count rejects
constant placement as this target's leading explanation, while leaving it a
broader loop/short-call tradeoff. Cold exception regions can instead enlarge
temporary capacity; their physical range still needs the separate validity
proof if entry initializes it unnecessarily.

Smallest experiment: account separately for header stores, newly NULLed tail,
constant-home fills, argument/default owners and actual locals cleared for
the two logging callees, including exact versus general entry. Compare the
typed-field cleanup with a source prototype of direct constant access on one
short nonescaping operation, before considering validity metadata. Inspect
the exposed/generator paths separately; they cannot borrow ordinary thread
assumptions.

Reject a broad frame redesign if repeated NULL work is already absent, if
constants/headers are a small fraction, or if alternate access costs cancel
entry savings. Any change that hides a live owner from GC/frame exposure or
changes finalizer order is invalid. Lazy/shared kwargs and early destruction
of user locals remain outside the admissible choices.

## Evidence needed for selection

The next decision should compare a single diagnostic account across A–F:
semantic calls and returns, mutually exclusive route outcomes, actual escape
phases, class branches, window transfers, initialized/cleared homes, dispatches,
and GCC spills/retired work. Use the real warm path and unchanged controls;
report diagnostics separately from release timings. No large implementation
is required to discover that a mechanism has little target coverage.

Require each candidate proposal to state what work vanishes, where that work
is currently executed, which invariant makes removal valid, and which result
would end the experiment. Select one coherent small discriminating increment
per mechanism under consideration before expanding scope. Keep the reviewed
tiny fixes available, but do not substitute their correctness for an
architectural answer or their source size for measured value. The coordinator
and user retain the batch-selection decision.

## Follow-up evidence: frame coverage resolved

The coordinator's native `frame-layout.json`, read independently after this
draft, identifies R5 `0953757f4e7` and reports:

| Callee | `nlocalsplus` | Temporary slots | Constant homes | Frame words, including header |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `Logger.debug` | 4 | 5 | 0 | 22 |
| `Logger.isEnabledFor` | 3 | 8 | 0 | 24 |

The header is 13 words by subtraction in both rows. The recorded local-kind
mapping contains no hidden constant homes. **Reject constant-pool relocation
as a logging-parity mechanism on this evidence.** It remains a broader IR
tradeoff for loop functions. This is a useful rejection before implementation,
not a reason to deny the alternative was architectural.

The eight temporary slots in `isEnabledFor` cover the whole function while
its warmed cache-hit prefix uses fewer. That establishes excess capacity
relative to this path, not eight avoidable initialization stores per call:
the current overlap can reuse a valid caller prefix. Account for the actual
new tail before considering validity metadata. The seven total user-local
homes across the two callees remain real owners or NULL; their observation
and destruction obligations do not vanish because the hot path is short.

Evidence storage is the coordinator-owned
`python-boil-the-ocean/build/pyjit-link-wave1/interpreter-parity-20261108/`.
The initial field-probe failure is retained there separately; this review
does not relabel it as a successful run. The coordinator also reports a new
six-round target baseline of 1.657289 with stable identities; its smaller
gap still requires about 39.7% candidate time reduction. The source alternatives
do not predict that result, and a baseline report is distinct from the two
campaign parity admission rule.

[Full V8 review](http://127.0.0.1:7878/s/xzzlxx17/artifacts/v8-interpreter-review) · [Alternatives comparison](http://127.0.0.1:7878/s/xzzlxx17/artifacts/interpreter-alternatives) · [Active plan](http://127.0.0.1:7878/s/xzzlxx17/artifacts/plan). Supporting relative links refer to the canonical checkout.

# Competing structural mechanisms for logging parity

2026-11-08. Design proposals, not implementation authorization. Runtime is
qualified R5 `0953757f4e7`; all references below are to that runtime unless
stated otherwise. No runtime source, generated product, build or native
workload was changed for this proposal. The coordinator selects a reviewed
batch after comparing this document with the call and compiler proposals.

## Decision supported by the source

Compare three mechanisms: checked leaf/escaping reader continuations,
observer-aware return/discard execution, and dictionary hit feedback. They
cover different work from specialized-call preparation. They share existing
canonical eight-byte homes and current 64-bit IR words; none requires an
accumulator, a second value representation or permanent experiment switches.

The strongest immediate discriminator is an exact-dictionary first-probe
identity-hit diagnostic, followed by a return-boundary diagnostic. The former
can distinguish dictionary lookup overhead from generic reader completion;
the latter can establish the cost and safe coverage of nine retained hot outer
POPs. Neither observation predicts the roughly 39.7% candidate-time reduction
needed from the new 1.657289 baseline. Sample shares cannot be added as gains.

Source already rejects part of an overbroad phase hypothesis. Generated
`LOAD_ATTR_METHOD_WITH_VALUES` has no reader refresh, and `LOAD_ATTR_SHAPE`
already publishes a canonical temporary result and refreshes only when its
receiver can deallocate. These are implemented mechanisms to reuse, not
missing optimizations. Their per-word PC stores and class/address calculations
remain possible machine-code questions, not proven redundant work.

## Evidence and common accounting

`E8` means the coordinator-owned evidence directory
`python-boil-the-ocean/build/pyjit-link-wave1/interpreter-parity-20261108/`.
Its `warmed-ir.json` establishes these sites, not dynamic branch counts:

| Body | Relevant ordinary path |
| --- | --- |
| Benchmark | Ten method loaders, message snapshots and general Python calls; nine retained hot POP continuations; the tenth call already discards |
| `Logger.debug` | Method load, module global load, exact Python call, false branch, None load, return |
| `Logger.isEnabledFor` | Shape load of `disabled`, boolean branch, shape load of `_cache`, dictionary subscription, return |

Correction to the earlier review's static count: `bench_silent` has ten POP
words in the capture, but one follows `truncate_stream` before the loop.
Inside the loop, the first nine calls have POP continuations; the tenth has
destination 4095 (`IR_NO_DST`) and goes straight to JUMP_BACKWARD. Thus the
coordinator's new R5 Py_STATS diagnostic showing nine POP dispatches per loop
agrees with this source. M2 has at most nine removable POP dispatches here;
the tenth call already exercises existing discard support. The diagnostic
also reports 161 total dispatches, 20 frames, ten general and ten exact calls,
20 method and 20 shape reads, ten dictionary subscriptions, ten message loads,
20 boolean branches and 20 returns per loop, with exact 2x scaling from 1,000
to 2,000 loops after empty subtraction. These are counts, not timing evidence.

`E8/frame-layout.json` gives debug 4 locals + 5 temporaries and isEnabledFor
3 + 8, zero constant homes in both, and a 13-word header. Constant-pool
relocation cannot remove per-call constant-home work on this target. Cold-path
temporary capacity is not proof of repeated initialization: count the new
tail after known-NULL overlap before proposing a validity map.

Preserve the following costs unless a particular proof removes them:

- Evaluated argument owners, fresh observable kwargs, parameter/default
  mapping, recursion, frame linkage and final local destruction.
- Mortal result acquisition and receiver/input decrements. A decrement that
  cannot deallocate is leaf work; it still changes an owner count.
- Publication before a possible callback, callback-current local semantics,
  precise error PC, monitoring activation, and refresh after an actual escape.
- Dictionary hash/equality calls that ordinary lookup would execute. A cache
  must preserve their effects, even if the dictionary itself does not mutate.

Keep diagnostic counters outside release timings. Attribute sites, semantic
lookups, input-retirement outcomes, frames, observer boundaries and actual
dispatches need separate denominators. Report overlaps between mechanisms.

## M1. Checked leaf and escaping reader continuations

**Question:** can a provider's proven nonescaping, canonical hit bypass generic
reader completion while retaining the same owner retirement and fault PC?
This applies to the dictionary hot path and later other checked readers; it
does not assert that all specialized handlers are leaf.

Actual before path, `Python/generated_ir_cases.c.h:2899`:

1. Publish the dictionary word as `frame->instr_ptr`; decode homes.
2. Guard the mapping provider against `_PyDict_Subscript`.
3. Consume temporary inputs or duplicate local inputs into held owners.
4. `value_subscript` rediscovers exact-dictionary type and calls
   `PyDict_GetValue`; this may hash, compare, pin inputs and execute Python.
5. `value_reader_complete` checks current frame/output, publishes the result,

`Python/ceval.c:value_subscript`, `value_reader_complete`,
`value_operation_refresh`; `Objects/dictobject.c:PyDict_GetValue`,
`_PyDict_GetValue_KnownHash`, `compare_generic` establish this behavior.

Proposed after path:

1. Keep the current instruction PC published. Retain conservative family
   effects and ordinary instrumentation. First prove a GIL-held exact dict,
   inline-int query, general combined table, and first probe whose stored key
   is the same canonical value and whose current value is non-NULL.
2. A dictionary-owned internal primitive duplicates the canonical current
   value and reports `HIT_LEAF`; it does not consume inputs, allocate, call
   user code, manufacture an exception, or retain table pointers. Every guard
   failure reports `DECLINE`, with no effects or new owner. The unchanged
   generic path handles decline, absence, subclasses and errors.
3. On hit, consume temporary inputs and keep locals borrowed or owned according
   to the existing checked input contract. Publish the result to a temporary
   destination before any retiring owner can deallocate. A local destination
   remains untouched until input retirement completes.
4. Retire key then container in the same order as today. Test `MayDealloc`
   immediately before each ordered close, after any earlier close. When that
   check is false, close this owner inline. On the first possible deallocation,
   move this owner and all remaining owners to the common escaping retirement
   helper, then refresh and reload exactly as today. If every check was false
   at its own close and no boxes exist, omit refresh and decoded-state reload.
   Never precompute all checks: two aliases at refcount two can each initially
   appear leaf, while the second ordered close actually deallocates.
5. Store a folded local only after that phase; retire its displaced owner
   through the existing rule. Omit the second temporary store because the
   checked first-output publication already installed the canonical owner.

This is deliberately not a cross-handler accumulator or wholesale delayed-PC
scheme. PC stores remain until asynchronous inspection, tracing, errors and
deoptimization have a separately reviewed contract. M1 first targets the
helper round trip, generic publication/checks and reloads on a proved phase.

**Shared interface.** Extend the existing result-publication contract in
`Tools/cases_generator/ir_generator.py`, rather than adding unchecked C hints.
One checked provider outcome supplies `canonical_owned_result` and
`no_escape_since_decode`. A common multi-input completion rule takes result,
ordered input owners, destination and boxes; it reuses the shape reader's
canonical temporary publication and conditional retirement. The generator
rejects use after an escaping helper, allocation, poll, frame switch, unknown
release or instrumentation callback. Joining a leaf and escaping edge drops
decoded-state facts unless both reestablish them. Generic whole-instruction
effect metadata remains conservative for copy propagation and recovery.

The first-probe primitive belongs in `Objects/dictobject.c`, with its internal
declaration in `Include/internal/pycore_dict.h`; dictionary layout/probe code
must not be copied into the interpreter. Use the existing inline-int hash
implementation, not a logging-level constant or hand-written hash rule.
Initially support the ordinary GIL build and decline on free-threaded builds.
No feedback layout change is required for this first form.

**Owner and observer proof.** At entry, every input home is canonical or NULL.
The frame owns the local query and any local container; temporary homes own
their inputs until the leaf provider returns. The provider cannot invalidate
those borrows. It creates exactly one result owner from the dictionary home,
including a real increment for mortal results. Consumption moves temporary
owners once and leaves NULL. A temporary result is visible before input
destruction; the local destination follows the old retirement order. The
multi-owner rule checks each owner against its current count immediately
before closing it; a possible callback invalidates leaf facts and routes all
remaining retirement through the existing refresh. Earlier closes may change
later owners' counts even without callbacks, so aliasing needs no exception
to this sequential rule.
An inline query is insufficient on its own: an earlier colliding custom key
could run equality. The first-probe identity guard excludes that omitted
comparison. Non-identity, changed layout, missing value and subclass behavior
all decline before input consumption. Generic errors retain their original
PC, restoration and KeyError behavior. No user local dies at its last read.

**Migration and discriminator.** Medium scope: dictionary primitive, checked
generator contract, one DSL handler, regenerated metadata/product, and focused
tests. Start by counting first-probe identity hits and retirement outcomes.
Inspect fixed-GCC code for the current completion/reload path. If coverage is
material, compare two temporary source candidates with identical hit guards:
(a) hit provider followed by current completion; (b) the same provider followed
by checked phase completion. Their difference isolates the phase mechanism
from lookup improvement. These are sequential source experiments, never
runtime switches in a shipped design.

Reject M1 if the apparent refreshes follow real escapes, first-probe coverage
is poor, guard/helper spills outweigh removed work, or a shared contract
requires handler-specific exceptions. Callback-mutated locals/instrumentation,
temporary versus local destinations, mortal values, last receiver owners,
collision callbacks, misses and exception unwind decide correctness. Include
aliased input owners whose final ordered close deallocates. Existing
shape/method leaf behavior cannot be reported as new savings.
