## M2. Execute the return/discard boundary without ordinary dispatch

**Question:** can common return execute a retained ordinary POP boundary
directly while preserving its PC and every observer activation case?

Before, `bytecodes.c:_RETURN_VALUE`, `ceval_macros.h:IR_STORE_RETURN`, and
`generated_ir_cases.c.h:RETURN_VALUE/POP_TOP`:

1. Take the child's return owner; emit return hooks; unlink and clear the
   child. Clearing locals/kwargs can execute Python and change observers.
2. Resume at the caller word after CALL, publish the result into return_slot,
   dispatch POP, publish its PC, consume and NULL its temporary home, close
   the result, then dispatch the following word.

`regcfg_passes.c:discard_region` intentionally retains the last POP on a call
line. Tracing enabled inside the callee must observe that line before the
next caller line. Blindly using IR_NO_DST or deleting the POP changes this.

Proposed after path keeps CALL, POP and their source/offset metadata intact:

1. Complete ordinary child return, including all child clearing and hooks.
   Resolve the caller's current continuation P and live return_slot afterward;
   do not carry a pre-callback observer or instruction proof across clearing.
2. The common return continuation checks that P is an ordinary unwrapped POP,
   its input is the same temporary return_slot, instrumentation is current,
   and no supported instruction/line observer, low-level trace or pending
   observation path needs that boundary. Initially decline on any uncertainty,
   generator/interpreter-entry return or special continuation.
3. For a result that cannot deallocate, execute the POP semantics directly:
   publish `frame->instr_ptr = P`, keep the destination NULL, close the held
   result owner once, and continue at P+1. Preserve required result
   canonicalization unless a checked return-result proof already supplies it.
   There is no callback or poll between these guards and boundary completion.
4. Otherwise publish into the original result home and dispatch P unchanged.
   The existing INSTRUMENTED_LINE/INSTRUCTION handler can call observers,
   process an exception or honor a callback's changed instruction pointer.

The first prototype excludes possibly deallocating results even when no
observer is currently active. A result finalizer may enable tracing, inspect
the caller or jump its line; retaining the original path makes that proof
independent. Logging's None result may satisfy the safe tag test, but its
actual count must be recorded. The decrement still occurs for a mortal result
that is known not to deallocate. Skipping its physical home installation is
safe only in this nonobservable span: that home starts and ends NULL, while
the C value owns the result until the ordinary POP retirement point.

**Shared interface and migration.** Add a generated common
`resume_call_result` continuation with explicit call PC, boundary PC and next
PC concepts, even if adjacent words derive the latter two. Initially invoke
it only from ordinary Python return. The compiler retains the POP; no new
word bits or call-window encoding is needed. The shared continuation may
later serve synchronous/native call completion, but only after preserving
its distinct input retirement, monitoring and periodic-check ordering. Do not
move those checks into the POP or implement a logging-specific handler.

Observer checks must use the runtime's actual instrumentation epoch and
handler-wrapper protocol; `tstate->tracing == 0` alone is not sufficient.
Reusing the style of `IR_SKIP_RESUME` needs review against per-code/local
events, instruction tracing and instrumentation-failure recovery. A callback
at the boundary may set f_lineno: fallback must retain the existing changed-PC
path, not call an observer and then force P+1. Exception return/unwind never
executes this normal-success shortcut.

Medium scope: return generator/macros and focused observer/owner tests, with
instrumentation changes only if the existing epoch guard cannot establish a
complete proof. This removes an ordinary dispatch and result-home store/clear;
it does not remove either Python call, frame lifetime, kwargs allocation or
the observer boundary. It is independent of call-preparation proofs.

**Discriminator and rejection.** Count normal returns whose live P is POP,
matching temporary destinations, result MayDealloc outcomes, installed or
changed observers after child clearing, and actual skipped dispatches. First
compare a return-continuation implementation that still stores/clears the
result home with one that omits that traffic; this separates dispatch from
home work. Keep virtual boundary execution counts distinct from dispatches.
Fixed-GCC code must show that checking P costs less than the removed path.

Tests must enable tracing/monitoring inside a callee and inside a child-local
destructor, preserve the caller call-line event and offsets, exercise f_lineno
jumps and observer errors, and return mortal values with weakref/finalizer
callbacks. Include native fallbacks and non-POP return destinations. Reject
if observers require reconstructing a deleted boundary, the fast path hides
another equivalent dispatch, its guard cost cancels the gain, or return-heavy
controls regress. No code or line metadata is deleted in this first design.

### M2b. Explicit no-op line boundaries on branch edges

The ten hot NOPs per loop are a second instance of the same observation
problem. `isEnabledFor` word 5 is the `try` line's NOP; the false `disabled`
branch lands there before the cache-read line. It has a source boundary even
though its normal execution performs no data operation. Removing the word
would remove the observer's location.

An alternative prototype retains that word and has the specific producer/
branch continuation execute its ordinary boundary inline. After evaluating
and retiring the exact boolean condition, resolve the live target P; check
current instrumentation and the ordinary NOP handler, publish P as the boundary
PC, then dispatch P+1. An instrumented target goes through its existing handler
and may change PC or raise. Preserve branch-monitoring behavior as well as the
line/instruction boundary. Any condition retirement that might call Python
must finish and invalidate/reestablish the proof before this check.

Select this edge through a generated branch form or compiler metadata for
explicit boundary targets. Do not add a speculative next-NOP test to every
DISPATCH. The ordinary word, offsets and wrapper protocol remain authoritative
when tracing starts after the branch form was selected. The contract is an
executed semantic boundary with an optional ordinary dispatch, not a deleted
source line. Distinguish ten candidate NOP dispatches from nine candidate POP
dispatches; do not combine their expected gains before separate prototypes.
Reject this variant if added branch/metadata checks replace the saved dispatch,
observer activation cannot recover the exact boundary, or the generalization
needs source-function exceptions. This may be cheaper to test than result-home
fusion because NOP has no result owner, but it does not measure POP home work.

## M3. Dictionary feedback with a no-callback probe-prefix proof

**Question:** beyond M1's direct first-probe hit, does stable keyed feedback
remove enough hashing/probing to justify new cache state?

The current dictionary specialization establishes only a builtin mapping
provider. `value_subscript` and `PyDict_GetValue` still perform full lookup;
the shared `_PyFbBinary` has type versions and an extension descriptor, not
a dict entry cache. A new feedback form is therefore an implementation and
metadata change, not an absent feature already encoded in the IR word.

Competing concrete designs:

| Design | Hit work | Constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 direct first probe | Inline-int hash, initial bucket lookup, current key/value guards | No feedback allocation or retained pointer; decline if the first candidate is not identical |
| M3 certified index | Query-value guard, general-table/nonzero keys-version guard, entry bounds/key/value guards | Cache fill must certify that skipped probes would execute no Python |
| Unqualified cached index | Version and final key check | Reject: can omit observable equality calls before the matching entry |

For the certified form, fill a small entry containing inline query value,
nonzero dictionary keys version and entry index only after checking the
ordinary probe prefix. Each skipped occupied entry must have a different
stored hash, or a proved native comparison with the same outcome. Initially
accept only differing hashes and unequal inline-int keys. A same-hash custom
key rejects caching; do not invoke its equality while obtaining a certificate.
The fill can simply decline and let ordinary lookup run once. Its read-only
scan must share dictionary probe code rather than invent another traversal.

An unchanged nonzero keys version then certifies the same probe prefix. Read
the entry's current value on every hit and duplicate its canonical owner;
never cache the result or an unowned keys/entry pointer. A value replacement
must return the new value. Key insertion, deletion, resize and clear invalidate
the proof through the keys-version rules. Version exhaustion (zero) declines.
Audit every structural mutation against `dictobject.c` before relying on this;
`_PyDictKeys_GetVersionForCurrentState` is a provider, not a blanket proof that
every consumer's desired invariant follows. Initially decline for split/
Unicode tables, subclasses, arbitrary object keys and free-threaded builds.

Stable key identity plus version alone is insufficient. A custom key before
the desired entry can have equality whose effects or answer change through
external state while the dictionary remains unchanged. Skipping it changes
Python behavior. The certificate removes this risk by excluding that callback
from the cached path at fill time and invalidating the structural proof on
every relevant table change.

Use the same checked canonical leaf-hit completion as M1; duplicate input
pinning and reader refresh may disappear only because that path cannot
escape. M3's lookup savings and M1's completion savings overlap and require
the two-candidate decomposition above. Dictionary input retirement still
falls back to escaping completion if it can deallocate. Misses and unsupported
cases preserve ordinary hash/equality order, __missing__, KeyError and unwind.

Medium to high scope: one binary-family feedback variant or an explicitly
owned side entry, producers/readers, cache clearing, generated metadata and
specialization/instrumentation tests. Do not reinterpret a live descriptor
pointer or enlarge every binary site's cache without accounting for footprint.
The current D feedback field can address a suitably generated entry; changing
the 64-bit instruction encoding is unnecessary. Prefer M1's smaller primitive
unless observed collisions/probe length show material additional coverage.

The cheapest discriminator counts exact-dict inline-int lookups by first-probe
identity, safe longer prefix, callback prefix, miss, table kind and version
churn. A diagnostic shadow certificate must neither call equality nor pin or
retain objects; coordinator-owned source instrumentation is sufficient.
Reject M3 as the next packet if first-probe hits already cover nearly all
useful cases, cache/version loads cost more than the short probe, safe prefixes
are uncommon, or metadata footprint/control regressions outweigh the benefit.
Adversarial collision equality, changing equality without dict mutation,
delete/reinsert, resize, value replacement and version exhaustion are decisive
correctness cases.

reference count or code lifetime. Test mortal/immortal executable ownership,
ordinary/overlap/generator/trampoline creation, exception clearing, frame
exposure and `code.replace` constants. Verify actual GCC removes the checks;
measure target and call/non-call controls before keeping performance-only
API complexity.

### 3. Remove the duplicate successful call-refresh validation

**Accept a small independent slice. Implementation defect.**

`R/Python/ceval.c:1422` calls `value_operation_refresh`, then immediately
`value_frame_is_current`. Successful refresh already checked the current frame,
executable, words and PC range, and no callback occurs between these checks.
An offline disassembly of the retained R5 ELF shows the duplicate executable
load/null/words checks at `0x333a3e–0x333a55`, after the successful PC store at
`0x333a38`; GCC has not removed them.

Return immediately on refresh success. Preserve the existing failure-path
second validation and error handling, because constructing an error can
escape. This leaves all actual post-escape validation and fault-PC publication
intact. V8's [call-aware state publication](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/63481c19453c72221531058be6d2e94adf3ebc66/src/interpreter/interpreter-assembler.cc#L751)
is the relevant comparison: publish where required, without redoing an
unchanged successful check. Test allocation/reentry and existing transaction
failure cases; inspect release GCC and count refreshes separately from calls.

### 4. Use phase contracts to reduce handler state traffic

**Accept bounded proposal work. Emitter/implementation opportunity; Python
observation remains a constraint.**

`R/Tools/cases_generator/ir_generator.py:2534–2605` flushes and reloads around
call preparations; `finish_value_operation` rereads word/slots after cleanup.
`IRStack.store:2039` and the R4/R5 result-phase work already distinguish
temporary publication from a folded-local store. The retained shape report
identifies two extra companion-slot address calculations on a local route.
Fix that known emitter dataflow first, using the shared flush preparation.

Then audit one hot helper sequence for an already-published PC/home or
unchanged decoded field with no intervening escape. Express the proven phase
in the shared checked contract and consume it locally. Keep the existing
whole-handler effects conservative; specialization can miss, and a folded
local's old-owner release can run Python. Do not infer purity merely from a
specialized opcode. V8's
[assembler](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/63481c19453c72221531058be6d2e94adf3ebc66/src/interpreter/interpreter-assembler.cc#L23)
tracks call invalidation and saves offsets according to call behavior.

Expected work removed: redundant address calculation, stores/reloads or
refreshes in a proved phase. No publication fact crosses a callback unless
the existing contract explicitly guarantees it. Admission must include
temporary/local/discarded destinations, object/scalar payloads, local writes
by callbacks, error ordering, line/monitor events and the generic path.

### 5. Make compiler equivalence ownership-aware before adding an accumulator

**Accept a bounded inventory; defer wider compiler changes pending evidence.
Compiler/IR policy constrained by Python ownership.**

`R/Python/regcfg_passes.c:240` folds single-reader borrowed local loads and
kills pending loads across possible Python execution or local writes. It
preserves source-line boundaries. `regcfg.c:898` also tracks dead-but-owned
temporaries and contiguous windows. These constraints explain why simply
borrowing caller locals or applying last-read liveness is unsafe.

V8's [equivalence optimizer](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/63481c19453c72221531058be6d2e94adf3ebc66/src/interpreter/bytecode-register-optimizer.cc#L322)
distinguishes materialization and observable registers, and materializes
register lists. Inventory the warmed logging IR's surviving moves and owner
duplicates by reason: semantic snapshot, window placement, observer boundary,
or avoidable compiler limitation. Start with a same-line, nonescaping region
whose immutable inline values or existing owning homes prove equivalence;
remove one transfer without changing destruction time. Do not weaken the
family-wide reentry kill or retain mortal borrowed locals across argument
evaluation.

Expected work removed only after such a proof: a dispatch or slot transfer,
possibly its duplicate count. Test local mutation through frames, argument
evaluation order, exceptions, line jumps and dead-but-owned loops. A new
cross-handler accumulator requires explicit roots/recovery and is deferred.

### 6. Assess operand-class and call-window costs with dynamic denominators

**Accept measurement; defer encoding changes. IR/layout constraint.**

`R/Include/internal/pycore_ir.h:20–106` reserves all 64 bits; fields identify
homes but do not encode local/temporary class. `ceval_macros.h:505–636`
therefore performs class-dependent consumption/publication. Calls also require
evaluated owning temporary windows. V8 has
[receiver/arity-specific bytecodes](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/63481c19453c72221531058be6d2e94adf3ebc66/src/interpreter/bytecodes.h#L293)
and lists; its smaller forms do not justify losing Python argument snapshots.

Count executed class tests, window-producing transfers and decoded operands
per hot semantic operation, separating temporary/local destinations and call
shapes. Compare with actual GCC to exclude tests already folded by the
generator. Only then design an encoding or handler refinement that eliminates
material work without multiplying a general call ABI. A new class bit would
trade slot range or another field; specialization/instrumentation currently
share operand layouts. Require an explicit range/large-function, branch,
instrumentation and generic-fallback migration plan before such a revision.
This is deferred behind recommendations 1–4.

### 7. Measure dispatch/footprint before changing the handler backend

**Accept evidence collection; defer backend and word-width rewrites.
Implementation and layout tradeoff.**

`R/Python/ceval_macros.h:64–106` passes five state arguments under GCC's
selected tail-call convention; it does not explicitly assign machine
registers. V8's [dispatch descriptor](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/63481c19453c72221531058be6d2e94adf3ebc66/src/codegen/interface-descriptors.h#L2432)
and [tail dispatch](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/63481c19453c72221531058be6d2e94adf3ebc66/src/interpreter/interpreter-assembler.cc#L1286)
make that machine interface explicit. Our fixed eight-byte word gives simple
decoding but spends space on absent operands; V8's
[operand scaling](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/63481c19453c72221531058be6d2e94adf3ebc66/src/interpreter/bytecode-operands.h#L59)
takes a different tradeoff.

For the warmed target, retain bytecode/feedback size, handler transitions and
GCC spill/reload sequences at hot helper boundaries. Normalize instructions
and branches by semantic operations and dispatches, with code-cache counters
treated cautiously. First remove a demonstrated spill or helper boundary
within current C/GCC generation. Introduce compact words or a custom handler
backend only if this evidence identifies a material remaining limit. Do not
change compiler or claim V8's generated-handler architecture proves C cannot
perform adequately. Test all dispatch, instrumented, stats and error targets
for any eventual interface change.

### 8. Keep native recovery separate and reuse baseline homes deliberately

**Accept architectural boundary; defer implementation to the selected JIT
workstream. Not a JIT-off parity optimization.**

The baseline already supplies physical canonical homes and fault PCs; future
optimizing code needs effect-prefix, owner and resume-state recovery beyond
those words. Follow the reviewed
[recovery contract](../../design/jit-e2e-system.md) rather than treating
baseline liveness as a root or deoptimization map. V8's historical
[Sparkplug design](https://v8.dev/blog/sparkplug) shows why compatible baseline
frames can simplify native entry and observation; it is not a reason to make
the baseline itself optimizing SSA.

The smallest later slice remains prepared owners plus shared once-only
transfer commit and forced native exits. Its work removal would be native
decode/dispatch elimination; it cannot count toward a JIT-disabled result.
Admission requires actual allocation failures, callback invalidation,
exceptions, exactly-once effects and monitoring during recovery. Preserve the
current interpreter as the semantic provider while this separate work proceeds.

## Concrete common-call preparation design for recommendation 1

Implement the smallest unbound specialized Python route first. Keep existing
word fields, return destinations, transaction status and generic provider.
The one conceptual division is **guarded facts → fallible preparation → final
guards → shared infallible commit**.

1. At `CALL_PY_GENERAL`, the function/version and PEP 523 guards establish an
   exact Python function before any escape. Mark method preparation complete
   using the existing `CALL_PREPARED` meaning; no method expansion is needed.
   Carry the exact-function fact to the private preparation entry. Do not
   infer it from the opcode name inside a generic provider or preserve it on
   a deopt/fallback edge that did not execute the guards.
2. Enter the same common positional preparation through a private checked
   function entry, using scalar arguments or a transaction record that stays
   in the out-of-line helper's C frame. Avoid taking a handler-local address.
   Generic CALL still discovers its provider and uses the same preparation
   routine after proving the required entry facts. Bound-method preparation
   keeps its existing refresh; its pre-expansion function version cannot be
   reused after wrapper retirement.
3. Check positional shape, executable and capacity before allocating. Retain
   the pinned selected code through allocating kwargs preparation. The initial
   type/hook/provider proof only avoids rediscovery up to this escape. For
   `CO_VARKEYWORDS`, allocate the required fresh empty dict and refresh the
   actual caller once. On error, preserve the existing owner/error path.
4. Revalidate all mutable entry facts after allocation: actual window callable
   and code identity, standard vectorcall, hook, executable/capacity, defaults
   coverage and self offset. Use a fresh view of the owning caller window.
   A guard decline releases prepared resources, refreshes, then enters the
   existing fallback once. A preparation/refresh failure stays an error.
5. Both entry routes reach one private nonescaping commit using the checked
   code and argument mapping. Reuse the existing overlap primitive and NULL
   proof. Transfer callable and arguments once; fill default owners, empty
   varargs and prepared kwargs; publish return slot and current child before
   any escaping release. No allocation, deopt, callback or failure may occur
   from first detachment to clearable child publication. Retain current
   recursion/RESUME, monitoring and child-not-started cleanup.

The implementation may first land only the existing `CALL_PREPARED` proof for
this specialized route, then remove provider rediscovery in a second reviewed
slice if GCC and dynamic counts justify it. Share the commit rather than
duplicating overlapping frame setup. The no-kwargs shortcut can reuse this
same commit later, but it is not the primary logging proposal.

The coordinator's warmed IR confirms `bench_silent`, `Logger.debug` and
`Logger.isEnabledFor` as described above. Next obtain separate stats-only
counts: direct exact, general specialized, expanded method,
accepted allocating/nonallocating overlap, each decline, consuming binder,
native, monitoring and error. Reconcile mutually exclusive outcomes. Source
predicts call shapes; samples do not establish their frequencies.

Expected work removed is finite and inspectable: unnecessary method tests,
duplicate pre-escape type/provider/hook tests, and any marshalling/spills that
the private entry actually eliminates. The post-allocation guards and frame
ownership work stay. Require fresh GCC disassembly, focused semantic tests,
balanced target/control timing and independent cold source/result review.
Keep the change only on correctness and measured benefit.

## Measurement review and limits

The coordinator's [plan](plan.md) has the right target, fixed workload and
JIT-off constraints. Two fresh six-round campaigns with GM at most 1.00 and
each round at most 1.02 are an empirical parity admission rule. Before capture,
fix the estimator as each process's arithmetic mean of all seven timings,
paired candidate/upstream ratio per round, then GM of six ratios. Balance
three upstream-first and three candidate-first rounds; retain the same fixed
loop count across both campaigns. Assert native CPU15 affinity immediately
before timed work in both roles. Retain all raw values, failures, identities
and load observations. Restart a rejected campaign into a new evidence
directory; do not replace selected rows. Report spread and both campaigns'
raw ratios. Passing this rule is repeatability evidence, not a statistical
proof that every execution is equivalent.

Review-only verification: read actual runtime source and retained GCC output,
checked R5 ELF identity, compared pinned primary V8 sources and read the
coordinator's warmed-IR capture. This reviewer ran no new native
workload, test, build or performance capture. Existing profiles cannot
assign elapsed cost to source checks or prove that these changes reach parity.

# V8 review and architectural comparison checkpoint

2026-11-08. The coordinator prioritized call preparation before completing a
comparative case. The user challenged that narrowing. Selection is now held
while the competing mechanisms are evaluated. The qualified runtime remains
R5 `0953757f4e7`; a three-line refresh cleanup is preserved only in the
isolated task worktree, uncommitted, unbuilt and untested.

## Eight recommendations and their scope

The [V8 review](v8-review.md) compares pinned primary sources with our actual
runtime, not an assumed missing frame stack. Its ranking is advisory; the
[decision ledger](recommendations.md) owns selection.

| Recommendation | Concrete opportunity | Current assessment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Preserve specialized call facts | Stop rediscovering type/provider/preparation facts before any escape; share final prepare/commit | Structural candidate. Does not remove fresh kwargs or post-allocation guards |
| Preserve known code-object types | Avoid generic numeric canonicalization at executable-home initialization | Small cleanup; correct shared tag and ownership domain required |
| Remove duplicate successful refresh validation | Successful refresh already proves current frame/code/PC | Small cleanup. Held diff preserves the potentially reentrant failure path |
| Model state publication by execution phase | Reuse published/canonical state until a callback or owner retirement invalidates it | Structural candidate; shape/method leaf behavior already exists |
| Make register equivalence ownership-aware | Place producers into final argument windows and remove avoidable transfer dispatches | Compiler candidate. Evaluated snapshots and destruction order remain required |
| Assess operand-class/window representation | Remove demonstrated local/temporary classification costs through generated forms or layout changes | IR candidate. Encoding changes need range, instrumentation and fallback migration |
| Improve dispatch/helper machine interface | Remove surviving spills/helper boundaries; consider observer-preserving fusion and density separately | Broad candidate under the same GCC. Compact words or a custom backend require evidence |
| Share recovery contracts with native execution | Reuse canonical homes, prepared owners and once-only effect/transfer state | Accepted future JIT boundary; cannot improve JIT-disabled parity |

Five are structural interpreter/compiler candidates, two are local cleanups,
and one belongs to the later JIT stage. Implementing the two small cleanups
would not constitute incorporating the architectural review.

## Concrete competing designs

The [independent alternatives review](alternatives-review.md) compares call
entry, publication phases, compiler/window construction, operand classes,
dispatch/fusion and frame/constant policy. A further Sol proposal and two
independent review rounds made three alternatives more concrete:

- A dictionary-owned leaf-hit primitive with checked generated completion,
  preserving canonical result ownership and sequential input retirement.
  Compare lookup savings separately from completion/reload savings. Also
  assess proven leaf temporary producers without assuming all PC stores can
  disappear.
- Return/result-discard and selected branch/NOP continuations that retain
  actual observer-boundary words and fallback paths. Recheck instrumentation
  after child clearing; a destructor can enable tracing. A complete observer
  predicate is still required before implementation.
- Dictionary feedback with a proved callback-free probe prefix. A stable
  keys version and matching final entry alone cannot justify skipping earlier
  collision equality callbacks. Mutation/version proofs remain open, and a
  cache may be unnecessary if the first probe already hits.

These designs are competing proposals, not accepted implementations or
additive speedup estimates. See [mechanisms](mechanisms-proposal.md),
[first review](mechanisms-peer-review.md) and
[second review](mechanisms-peer-review-round2.md).

## Measured starting point

The independently checked six-round pinned `logging_silent` baseline is
**1.657289x upstream**, with ratios spanning 1.636744–1.689003. Matching it
requires about **39.7% less candidate elapsed time**. It is a different
protocol from the older 1.743034 result, with no runtime source improvement
between them. The prior qualified perf campaign found 1.720317x instructions
and 1.629600x cycles per workload loop; those counters are different
measurements and are not per-bytecode ratios.

Existing stats, independently checked against raw dumps and exact input
scaling, give **161 dispatches and 20 frames per loop**: ten general calls,
ten exact calls, twenty method loads, twenty shape loads and ten dictionary
subscriptions. Nine result POPs and ten line-boundary NOPs execute. The tenth
logging result is already discarded; the extra static POP inventory site
belongs to pre-loop setup. Dispatch shares do not measure elapsed savings.
Both hot callees have zero constant homes; frame constant relocation does not
address this workload.

The runtime already has frame stacks, known-NULL overlap reuse and locals-only
ordinary clearing. Constant copying does not occur in these hot callees.
Further frame work must address actual remaining setup/retirement. Evidence
supports investigation of repeated entry work, generic helper completion and
dispatch/state overhead. It does
not yet assign a causal fraction to any of them. See
[diagnostic results](diagnostic-results.md) and
[independent baseline audit](baseline-evidence-review.md).

## Next gate

Use bounded diagnostics and release GCC inspection to compare covered machine
work, semantic proof, shared implementation cost and regression risk. Resolve
the observer and dictionary proof obligations before implementing those
mechanisms. Select the next coherent batch in the ledger, document why other
alternatives wait, then follow the normal implementation, focused checks,
post-review and integration cycle. Preserve target/control timing at integration
and full qualification at the coherent runtime checkpoint. No parity or new
runtime performance gain is claimed at this design-comparison checkpoint.
